rows.note: This is the all-purpose verb for moving or walking on foot, including going a short distance.

example.english: Step forward a little; I can't see.
example.jyutping: nei5 haang4 cin4 siu2 siu2 ngo5 tai2 m4 dou2

rows.note: Use this for a distinct stage or phase in a process; it is the all-purpose choice for this sense.

example.english: This is a step in the reform.
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 hai6 goi2 gaak3 ge3 gaai1 dyun6

rows.note: Use this for one movement from one foot to the other or the distance covered by that movement.

example.english: Take one step first and see if it is wide enough.
example.traditional: 行一步先，睇下夠唔夠闊。
example.jyutping: haang4 jat1 bou6 sin1 tai2 haa5 gau3 m4 gau3 fut3

rows.note: Use this specifically for a step on a staircase, rather than a pace or a process stage.

example.jyutping: siu2 sam1 di1 tai1 kap1 hou2 sin3

rows.note: Use this specifically for a rung or crossbar on a ladder, not for a staircase step.

example.english: Make sure your foot is firm on the step before climbing.
example.traditional: 踩穩條梯嘅橫檔先好上。
example.jyutping: caai2 wan2 tiu4 tai1 ge3 waang4 dong2 sin1 hou2 soeng5

rows.note: Use this when the thing being put on is trousers; Cantonese normally expresses putting them on without retaining the stepping manner.

example.english: Step into your trousers quickly, or you'll be late.
example.traditional: 你快啲著褲，唔係就遲到喇。
example.jyutping: nei5 faai3 di1 zoek3 fu3 m4 hai6 zau6 ci4 dou3 laa3
